title: Add hold keypad feature (key 3) to move app container position
description:
The app container is currently in a fixed position and not customizable. Add a new hold keypad feature using key 3 that allows users to:

1. Enter 'move mode' by holding key 3
2. Move the app container/dialog to their preferred screen position
3. Save the position preference using SharedPreferences
4. Restore the saved position on future app launches

This improves accessibility and user customization for different device sizes and user preferences.
close_reason: Feature implemented: Hold key 3 to enter move mode, drag to reposition dialog, position saved to SharedPreferences

title: Landscape and portrait positions should be saved separately
description:
Currently, the saved dialog position is shared between landscape and portrait orientations. This causes issues because:

1. A position that works well in portrait may be off-screen in landscape
2. User preferences for position likely differ between orientations
3. Screen dimensions change significantly between orientations

Solution: Store separate position preferences:
- dialog_x_portrait, dialog_y_portrait, has_custom_position_portrait
- dialog_x_landscape, dialog_y_landscape, has_custom_position_landscape

Load appropriate position based on current orientation in onCreate() and onConfigurationChanged().

title: Move mode only allows horizontal dragging
description:
When in move mode, the dialog can only be dragged horizontally. Vertical movement is not working or severely restricted.

Expected: Dialog should move freely in both X and Y directions.
Actual: Only horizontal (X-axis) movement works.

title: App container size inconsistent across device aspect ratios
description:
The app container appears squished (smaller width) on mobile phones compared to tablets. The dialog-style window sizing varies based on device aspect ratio, leading to inconsistent user experience.

**Current Behavior:**
- On tablets: Container appears at expected width
- On mobile phones: Container appears narrower/squished

**Expected Behavior:**
- Fixed container size across all device aspect ratios
- Consistent visual experience regardless of device form factor

**Technical Context:**
- App uses dialog-style window (see T9Activity.kt)
- Need to investigate WindowManager and layout constraints

comments.author: android
comments.text:
## Fix Applied

Changed themes.xml:12-13 from percentage to fixed dp:
- windowMinWidthMajor: 70% → 320dp
- windowMinWidthMinor: 70% → 320dp

This ensures consistent dialog width across all device aspect ratios.

title: Research Android WindowManager APIs for fixed dialog sizing
description:
Research how Android WindowManager handles dialog window dimensions and how to set fixed sizes that ignore device aspect ratio.

**Research Areas:**
- WindowManager.LayoutParams for dialog windows
- setLayout() with fixed dimensions vs percentage-based
- Display metrics and density-independent pixels (dp)
- Theme-based window sizing (windowMinWidthMajor/Minor)

comments.author: android
comments.text:
## Research Complete

**Solution: Use fixed dp values instead of percentages**

Replace percentage-based sizing with fixed dp:
- android:windowMinWidthMinor: 320dp
- android:windowMinWidthMajor: 320dp

Or use windowFixedWidth attributes for truly fixed sizing:
- android:windowFixedWidthMinor: 320dp
- android:windowFixedWidthMajor: 320dp

**Key insight**: windowMinWidthMinor = portrait mode, windowMinWidthMajor = landscape mode. Using the same dp value ensures consistency across all devices.

title: Research best practices for consistent dialog UI across form factors
description:
Research Android design guidelines and community best practices for maintaining consistent dialog dimensions across phones and tablets.

**Research Areas:**
- Material Design guidelines for dialogs
- Common patterns used by popular apps
- Responsive vs fixed sizing trade-offs
- Accessibility considerations for fixed sizes

comments.author: android
comments.text:
## Best Practices Research

**Material Design Recommendations:**
- Dialogs should have consistent, predictable sizing
- Fixed widths work well for launcher-style apps
- Common fixed widths: 280dp (compact), 320dp (medium), 360dp (comfortable)

**Recommended approach for T9 Dialer:**
- Use ~320dp fixed width (fits 3 app icons comfortably)
- Same value for both portrait and landscape
- Consider max width cap for very large screens

**Trade-offs:**
- Fixed size: Consistent UX but may waste space on tablets
- Percentage: Adaptive but inconsistent across devices
- Recommendation: Fixed is better for this apps compact UI goal

title: Move mode UX is unintuitive - needs better interaction design
description:
Current implementation: Long-press key 3 enters move mode, drag anywhere, release to save position.

Issues with current UX:
- Single long-press to enter, release to save is confusing
- No clear visual feedback during move mode
- Accidental position saves when user just wants to explore

Proposed improvement: Hold to activate draggable mode, then hold again to save/confirm position.

Need UI/UX designer input for better interaction pattern.

comments.author: android
comments.text:
## UI/UX Designer Recommendations

### Recommended Pattern: Press-Hold-Drag-Release

1. **Hold Button 3** → Enter move mode with visual feedback (border highlight)
2. **While holding, drag anywhere** → Dialog follows finger
3. **Release on Button 3** → Save position
4. **Release elsewhere** → Cancel and revert to previous position

### Why This Is Better
- Matches drag-and-drop conventions users already know
- Single continuous gesture (no need to reposition thumb)
- Prevents accidental saves (release location determines outcome)
- Clear cancel mechanism built-in

### Visual Feedback During Move Mode
1. **Border highlight**: Change mainCard stroke to accent color, increase to 3dp
2. **Button 3 highlight**: Change background to accent color
3. **Status indicator**: Show 'Drag to reposition' text

### Implementation Changes Needed
- Store previous position before drag starts (for cancel/revert)
- Add isTouchOnButton3() helper to detect release location
- Add visual feedback in enterMoveMode()
- Modify ACTION_UP handler to check release location

### Cancel Logic
```kotlin
MotionEvent.ACTION_UP -> {
    val save = isTouchOnButton3(ev)
    if (save) {
        savePositionPreference()
        Toast.makeText(this, "Position saved", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
    } else {
        // Revert to previous position
        dialogX = savedDialogX
        dialogY = savedDialogY
        applyDialogPosition()
        Toast.makeText(this, "Move cancelled", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
    }
    exitMoveMode()
}
```

### Additional Enhancements (Phase 2)
- Haptic feedback on enter/exit
- Snap-to-edges for easier positioning
- Position presets for quick switching

comments.author: android
comments.text:
## Research Findings: Implementation Approach for Movable App Container

### Current Codebase Analysis

**Window Positioning (T9Activity.kt:85-88):**
```kotlin
val isLandscape = resources.configuration.orientation == ...
window?.setGravity(if (isLandscape) Gravity.BOTTOM or Gravity.END else Gravity.BOTTOM)
```

**Existing Long-Press Patterns (T9Activity.kt:511-520):**
- Button 1: Long-press opens icon pack selector
- Button 2: Long-press toggles theme

**Touch Event Handling (T9Activity.kt:115-137):**
- dispatchTouchEvent() already handles outside-card detection
- Uses MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN and getLocationOnScreen()

**SharedPreferences Usage (T9Activity.kt:160-180):**
- Prefs name: "T9Dialer"
- Pattern: getSharedPreferences/putBoolean/putString/getString

### Implementation Approach

**1. Add Position Preference Keys:**
```kotlin
private var dialogX: Int = 0
private var dialogY: Int = 0
private var isMoveModeActive = false
```

**2. Load/Save Position in SharedPreferences:**
```kotlin
private fun loadPositionPreference() {
    val prefs = getSharedPreferences("T9Dialer", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
    dialogX = prefs.getInt("dialog_x", 0)
    dialogY = prefs.getInt("dialog_y", 0)
}

private fun savePositionPreference() {
    val prefs = getSharedPreferences("T9Dialer", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
    prefs.edit()
        .putInt("dialog_x", dialogX)
        .putInt("dialog_y", dialogY)
        .apply()
}
```

**3. Apply Position via WindowManager.LayoutParams:**
```kotlin
private fun applyDialogPosition() {
    window?.let { win ->
        val params = win.attributes
        params.gravity = Gravity.TOP or Gravity.START // Absolute positioning
        params.x = dialogX
        params.y = dialogY
        win.attributes = params
    }
}
```

**4. Add Long-Press Handler for Button 3:**
```kotlin
findViewById<MaterialButton>(R.id.btn3).setOnLongClickListener {
    enterMoveMode()
    true
}
```

**5. Move Mode Implementation:**
- Show visual indicator (toast or overlay text)
- Modify dispatchTouchEvent to handle drag gestures in move mode
- Track initial touch position and delta movement
- Update window position using WindowManager.updateViewLayout() or window.attributes

**6. Touch Drag Logic:**
```kotlin
private var initialTouchX = 0f
private var initialTouchY = 0f
private var initialX = 0
private var initialY = 0

override fun dispatchTouchEvent(ev: MotionEvent): Boolean {
    if (isMoveModeActive) {
        when (ev.action) {
            MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> {
                initialTouchX = ev.rawX
                initialTouchY = ev.rawY
                initialX = dialogX
                initialY = dialogY
                return true
            }
            MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE -> {
                dialogX = initialX + (ev.rawX - initialTouchX).toInt()
                dialogY = initialY + (ev.rawY - initialTouchY).toInt()
                applyDialogPosition()
                return true
            }
            MotionEvent.ACTION_UP -> {
                savePositionPreference()
                exitMoveMode()
                return true
            }
        }
    }
    // existing outside-card detection...
}
```

### Sources
- [WindowManager.LayoutParams](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/WindowManager.LayoutParams)
- [Floating Windows: Moving Window](https://dev.to/localazy/5-floating-windows-on-android-moving-window-1192)
- [Dialog Position in Android](https://www.tutorialspoint.com/how-to-change-the-position-of-the-dialog-on-screen-android-using-kotlin)

### Compatibility Notes
- WindowManager.LayoutParams.x/y work on SDK 23+ with absolute gravity (TOP|START)
- updateViewLayout() needed for real-time position updates
- SharedPreferences is safe for storing int values across SDK versions

comments.author: android
comments.text:
## Analysis Complete

**Root Cause Identified in themes.xml:12-13**

The dialog uses percentage-based sizing:
- windowMinWidthMajor: 70%
- windowMinWidthMinor: 70%

Minor axis (portrait/phones): 70% of narrow screen = squished
Major axis (landscape/tablets): 70% of wider screen = normal width

No programmatic sizing found in T9Activity.kt - window size is purely theme-driven.
